hero.title: Midday News & Global Update — Friday 13 November 2026
hero.description: Microsoft service disruption, Ukraine diplomacy, Nigeria's 2027 election dispute, global energy outlook, European AI competitiveness and verified opportunities.
hero.marquee: GLOBAL UPDATE: Microsoft 365 outage affects public services | IEA forecasts oil-market surplus | ADC receives court judgment copy | EU leaders debate AI competitiveness

morningSummary: Friday's midday agenda is dominated by a global Microsoft 365 disruption affecting Outlook, Teams and other services, with healthcare, police, schools and government organisations among those reporting problems. Microsoft says a patch is producing early signs of stabilisation, but recovery is incomplete. In Dublin, European leaders are debating who should represent the continent in future Ukraine peace talks and how Europe can strengthen its artificial-intelligence industry. The International Energy Agency now expects global oil supply to exceed demand in the fourth quarter as Gulf exports recover, although shipping risks remain. In Nigeria, the ADC has received the certified copy of the court judgment affecting its leadership and Atiku Abubakar's nomination process; the party's next legal steps and any INEC action will be closely watched. France's 2027 presidential contenders are divided over whether to boycott or appear on CNews. Germany's 2027 budget plan includes more than €210 billion in new borrowing. The edition also retains verified jobs, scholarships, grants and training opportunities with official application links and approaching deadlines.
breaking: GLOBAL TECHNOLOGY — Microsoft 365 services remain in staged recovery after a widespread outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and public services in several countries. Microsoft says it has no evidence of a cyberattack.
ENERGY — The IEA forecasts global oil supply will exceed demand by 1.7 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter, despite continuing Gulf shipping risks.
NIGERIA — The ADC has received the certified copy of the judgment affecting its leadership structure and Atiku Abubakar's nomination process; legal next steps are expected.
EUROPE — EU leaders are debating who should represent Europe in the next Ukraine peace negotiations.
EUROPE / TECHNOLOGY — Leaders are discussing AI investment, competitiveness and regulation at a Dublin summit.

featured.title: Microsoft 365 Outage Exposes the Risks of Dependence on a Few Global Technology Providers
featured.summary: A disruption to Outlook, Teams and other services has affected public agencies, healthcare, schools and businesses. Recovery is under way, but the incident raises questions about digital resilience.
featured.content:
A widespread Microsoft 365 disruption that began on Thursday evening has affected users and organisations across Europe, North America and Asia-Pacific. Services affected include Outlook, Teams and Copilot, with knock-on effects for public agencies and businesses that depend on Microsoft's cloud and communications systems.

The Guardian's live reporting says UK healthcare organisations, pharmacies, police online reporting services, schools and financial regulators have experienced disruption. In Australia and Japan, government agencies have also reported problems. Microsoft has attributed the incident to issues involving server configuration and traffic management and said it does not believe it is dealing with a cyberattack.

The company says a software patch has produced early signs of improved server stability, but service capacity remains below normal and recovery is continuing in stages. Organisations have been advised to use contingency channels where digital communications remain unavailable.

WHY IT MATTERS: The outage illustrates how concentration of essential services in a small number of cloud and productivity providers can create systemic operational risks. Healthcare, public safety, transport and financial services need tested fallback procedures.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch Microsoft's service-status updates, confirmation that delayed email and collaboration queues have cleared, and whether regulators or major customers call for stronger resilience requirements.
featured.source: Microsoft service updates; The Guardian; affected public agencies

topStories.title: EU Leaders Turn to AI Competitiveness as Dublin Summit Debates Funding and Regulation
topStories.summary: European leaders are discussing how the bloc can close the gap with the United States and China in artificial intelligence, while balancing investment, innovation and safeguards.
topStories.content:
European Union leaders are meeting in Dublin for discussions on artificial intelligence at a time when policymakers are concerned that Europe is falling behind the United States and China in the scale of AI investment and commercial deployment. Reuters reports that the agenda includes funding, competitiveness and the policy conditions needed to support the sector.

The debate is not only about research. It concerns access to computing infrastructure, energy, data, skilled workers, venture capital and the ability of European firms to scale products globally. Governments also face pressure to ensure that AI deployment respects privacy, safety, competition and labour protections.

The summit takes place alongside wider European discussions about Ukraine and continental security, highlighting how technology policy is increasingly linked to economic resilience and strategic autonomy.

WHY IT MATTERS: AI is becoming a major determinant of productivity, industrial competitiveness and national security. If Europe cannot scale its own companies and infrastructure, it may become more dependent on foreign platforms and suppliers.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for concrete funding commitments, cross-border infrastructure initiatives and any agreement on how the EU will simplify rules without weakening safeguards.

topStories.title: IEA Sees Global Oil Market Returning to Surplus Despite Continuing Gulf Shipping Risks
topStories.summary: The International Energy Agency now expects fourth-quarter supply to exceed demand by about 1.7 million barrels per day as Gulf exports recover, although attacks and disruption risks remain.
topStories.content:
The International Energy Agency says the global oil market is expected to return to surplus in the fourth quarter of 2026. In its November report, the Paris-based agency forecast average supply of 105 million barrels per day, around 1.7 million barrels per day above expected demand.

The outlook marks a change from the agency's earlier forecast of a deficit. Gulf producers are restoring exports after disruption linked to the conflict involving Iran, including through alternative shipping practices in the Strait of Hormuz. OPEC+ crude output also rose in October, reaching about 97 per cent of its pre-war February level.

The IEA said 71 million barrels from emergency reserves pledged by member countries would be made available by the end of February, including 15 million barrels of diesel. It also expects production growth from the United States, Canada, Brazil, Argentina and Guyana.

WHY IT MATTERS: A supply surplus could ease price pressure for consumers and import-dependent economies, but the outlook remains vulnerable to renewed attacks or a closure of key shipping routes. For Nigeria, oil prices influence export earnings, public revenue, foreign exchange and budget assumptions.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Monitor actual Gulf export volumes, tanker movements, OPEC+ production and whether the forecast surplus translates into lower prices.

topStories.title: Germany's Budget Committee Agrees 2027 Spending Plan with More Than €210 Billion in New Borrowing
topStories.summary: Reuters reports that lawmakers have agreed a draft 2027 federal budget involving more than €210 billion in new borrowing, one of the country's largest post-war debt-financed budgets.
topStories.content:
Germany's budget committee has agreed the 2027 federal budget, including more than €210 billion in total new borrowing, according to people familiar with the discussions cited by Reuters. The amount would be the second-highest level of new borrowing since the Second World War.

The spending plan reflects pressure to finance defence, infrastructure and other public priorities while Germany faces weak growth and a changing European security environment. The scale of borrowing is likely to intensify debate about fiscal rules, the sustainability of public finances and how quickly investment can translate into stronger economic performance.

The committee agreement is an important parliamentary step, but the final budget process and implementation will determine how much funding reaches projects and services.

WHY IT MATTERS: Germany is Europe's largest economy. Its spending decisions affect regional demand, defence procurement, infrastructure investment and the wider euro-area outlook.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch the Bundestag process, final spending allocations, borrowing costs and the government's ability to deliver the promised investment.

topStories.title: ADC Receives Certified Judgment Copy as Opposition Party Weighs Legal Next Steps
topStories.summary: Premium Times reports that the ADC has received the certified copy of the judgment affecting its leadership structure and Atiku Abubakar's nomination process. The party says it is considering its legal response.
topStories.content:
The African Democratic Congress has received the certified true copy of the Federal High Court judgment delivered on 5 November concerning the party's leadership structure, according to a report by Premium Times published on Friday. The document is significant because the party needs the court record to pursue any appeal or other lawful application.

The ruling has created uncertainty around the David Mark-led leadership and decisions taken under that structure, including the process that produced former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar as the party's presidential candidate. The precise legal consequences, including the status of the nomination and any interim relief, must be determined from the judgment itself and subsequent court orders.

INEC has previously said it will comply with binding court decisions and that it must act within the law. The commission's position should not be mistaken for a final judicial determination of Atiku's eligibility.

WHY IT MATTERS: The dispute affects opposition-party organisation, candidate selection and the legal timetable ahead of the 2027 elections. It also raises questions about how quickly pre-election disputes can be resolved.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for the ADC's formal appeal filings, any application for a stay, hearing dates and official INEC action based on the court record.
topStories.source: Premium Times; INEC statements; court proceedings

topStories.title: CBN Reports Further Inflation Easing, but Households and Businesses Still Face Cost Pressures
topStories.summary: A CBN official says headline inflation eased to 14.63 per cent in September, while warning that high living and operating costs continue to weigh on households and firms.
topStories.content:
A Central Bank of Nigeria official has said headline inflation fell to 14.63 per cent in September 2026, continuing a decline from the peak recorded in late 2024. The figure was highlighted during discussions at the Lagos International Trade Fair, according to Nigerian media reports.

The easing in the headline rate is an important macroeconomic development, but it does not mean prices have returned to earlier levels. Families continue to pay for food, transport, housing, energy and healthcare at prices that have accumulated during the inflationary period. Businesses also face financing, logistics and power costs.

The distinction between a slower rate of price increases and an actual fall in prices is essential when assessing the impact on living standards. A sustained improvement will depend on food supply, exchange-rate stability, energy costs, productivity and confidence in economic policy.

WHY IT MATTERS: Inflation affects purchasing power, wage negotiations, interest rates and business planning. A lower rate can improve confidence, but the benefits are felt only when household incomes and essential costs become more manageable.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Monitor the next National Bureau of Statistics inflation release, food-price trends and the CBN's policy decisions.
topStories.source: Central Bank of Nigeria; Nigerian newspaper reports

topStories.title: French Presidential Contenders Face a Campaign Dilemma over CNews and Media Pluralism
topStories.summary: Le Monde reports that parties across the political spectrum are divided over whether to boycott or appear on CNews, as the 2027 presidential campaign takes shape.
topStories.content:
French politicians are debating how to engage with CNews, the television channel owned by Vincent Bolloré, ahead of the 2027 presidential election. A petition calling for the channel to be banned attracted more than one million signatures, but the National Assembly declined to hold a debate on the issue, Le Monde reports.

The dispute exposes a wider political dilemma. Some left-wing figures argue that appearing on the channel legitimises an editorial line they consider biased; others say candidates should not abandon a large audience. The centrist camp is also divided, while right-wing and National Rally figures have defended access to the platform and media pluralism.

The debate involves questions of editorial independence, media regulation, political access and the role of powerful media owners in an election campaign. CNews has faced sanctions from the media regulator ARCOM for breaches of broadcasting rules, according to Le Monde.

WHY IT MATTERS: Media access and pluralism shape how voters encounter political arguments. The issue is especially important in a campaign where candidates are competing to define immigration, identity, security and economic policy.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch whether parties formalise appearance or boycott policies and whether ARCOM takes further regulatory action.

topStories.title: Europe Debates Who Should Represent It in Ukraine Peace Negotiations
topStories.summary: EU leaders in Dublin agree that Europe must have a voice in the next round of talks, but remain divided over whether to appoint one envoy or a wider negotiating team.
topStories.content:
European leaders are discussing how the continent should be represented in negotiations involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States. At the Dublin summit, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US envoy Jared Kushner said Europe would have a role in the next round of talks, but EU governments have not agreed on who should speak for them.

Italy's Giorgia Meloni has argued for a single authoritative representative, while Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin says the process must include non-EU partners such as the United Kingdom and Norway. Other possible options include senior EU officials, the E3 group of France, Germany and Britain, or a broader coalition.

Russia has opposed direct European involvement, while Ukraine wants its European partners present to help protect its security interests. The debate is therefore not simply procedural: it concerns the future security architecture of Europe and the credibility of any eventual settlement.

WHY IT MATTERS: A peace framework negotiated without the countries expected to support Ukraine's security could be difficult to implement. Europe's internal divisions may also weaken its influence.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for agreement on a representative or team, the next negotiating date and the conditions attached to any prisoner exchange or ceasefire proposal.

topStories.title: DR Congo Ebola Response Faces Continued Obstacles as Attacks Disrupt Health Work
topStories.summary: Health authorities and international partners face security and access challenges in eastern DR Congo, where attacks on responders are undermining outbreak-control work.
topStories.content:
The response to the Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo continues to face serious operational challenges. Reuters has reported warnings from Africa CDC that attacks on health workers and facilities are disrupting surveillance, treatment and community engagement.

Outbreak control depends on rapid case identification, safe treatment, contact tracing, vaccination where indicated and trust between health teams and local communities. Insecurity makes each of these tasks more difficult and can allow transmission chains to remain undetected.

The humanitarian situation is also complicated by displacement and limited access to affected areas. Health agencies need sustained support and safe access to carry out their work.

WHY IT MATTERS: Ebola outbreaks can spread beyond local communities when response systems are disrupted. Protecting health workers is a public-health necessity, not only a security concern.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch for updated case and death figures from health authorities, access improvements and additional protection for medical teams.
topStories.source: Africa CDC; Reuters; World Health Organization

topStories.title: US Inflation Debate Continues as Federal Reserve Weighs Persistent Price Pressures
topStories.summary: New York Fed President John Williams says more work is needed to bring inflation back to target, keeping the outlook for interest rates in focus.
topStories.content:
New York Federal Reserve President John Williams has said more work remains to bring inflation back to the central bank's target, according to Reuters. The comments come as policymakers assess price pressures, employment conditions and the strength of the US economy.

For households and companies, the direction of interest rates affects mortgages, credit-card costs, business investment and the dollar. Markets are weighing whether inflation will ease sufficiently to allow policy to remain steady or whether further tightening could be considered.

The Federal Reserve's decisions also influence global financial conditions, capital flows and borrowing costs in emerging markets.

WHY IT MATTERS: US monetary policy has global consequences. Changes in interest-rate expectations can affect currencies, commodity prices and the cost of financing for governments and businesses.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch upcoming US inflation and employment data, Federal Reserve communications and market expectations for the next policy meeting.
topStories.source: Reuters; Federal Reserve Bank of New York

topStories.title: Japan's Defence Spending Plans Face Budget Pressure as Suppliers Await Orders
topStories.summary: Reuters reports that proposed five-year defence spending may fall short of earlier expectations, potentially affecting planned orders for missiles and aircraft.
topStories.content:
Japan's defence procurement plans are facing pressure from budget constraints, with officials warning suppliers that some proposed orders could be reduced. Reuters reports that the government has not made a final decision on the detailed plan.

Japan has been increasing its defence capabilities in response to a more challenging regional security environment. However, higher spending commitments compete with other fiscal priorities, and procurement plans depend on the government's ability to fund and deliver equipment over several years.

The uncertainty matters for domestic manufacturers and international suppliers that rely on predictable multi-year orders.

WHY IT MATTERS: Japan's defence choices influence security calculations in East Asia and the wider Indo-Pacific, as well as industrial supply chains.

WHAT HAPPENS NEXT: Watch the final budget allocations, procurement decisions and any revisions to Japan's five-year defence programme.

leadersWatch.title: Leaders Watch
leadersWatch.description: Profiles of political and institutional leaders whose decisions are shaping international affairs. Reports distinguish confirmed decisions from political statements, allegations and unresolved legal questions.

leaders.name: Donald Trump
leaders.headline: US diplomacy on Ukraine and Iran keeps Washington at the centre of global security debates
leaders.report: US envoys have met Vladimir Putin and then Volodymyr Zelenskyy as Washington seeks to restart Ukraine negotiations. The administration is also maintaining its blockade on Iranian oil shipments.
leaders.background: The administration is balancing diplomatic efforts, military commitments, energy security and domestic economic pressures.
leaders.implications: The credibility of US diplomacy will depend on whether talks produce humanitarian progress and reduce escalation risks.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Statements from all parties should be tested against confirmed agreements, implementation and independently verified developments.
leaders.source: Associated Press; Reuters; White House statements

leaders.name: Emmanuel Macron
leaders.headline: France balances European security leadership with domestic economic and social pressures
leaders.report: France is participating in European discussions on Ukraine and continental security while the government faces continuing public debate over wages, purchasing power and social policy.
leaders.background: The domestic debate is unfolding ahead of the 2027 presidential contest and amid pressure on public finances.
leaders.implications: France's influence in Europe depends on both diplomatic engagement and domestic political stability.
leaders.radiantWavesView: International leadership should be considered alongside measurable progress on household costs, public services and economic confidence.

leaders.name: Bola Ahmed Tinubu
leaders.headline: 2027 election preparations face scrutiny over funding, technology and legal disputes
leaders.report: INEC says it will test accreditation and electronic result transmission in a nationwide mock exercise on 28 November. The commission also says it is dealing with more than 300 pending court cases.
leaders.background: The electoral process includes disputes over party leadership, voter-register concerns, election funding and security.
leaders.implications: Public confidence will depend on transparent procedures, timely funding and equal application of the law.
leaders.radiantWavesView: RadiantWaves will assess government and opposition claims against official records, court decisions and verifiable electoral safeguards.

leaders.name: Atiku Abubakar
leaders.headline: INEC says Atiku's eligibility will be governed by binding court decisions
leaders.report: INEC chairman Joash Amupitan says the commission is constitutionally required to obey court orders concerning Atiku's eligibility and the ADC leadership dispute.
leaders.background: The dispute remains within the legal process. ADC has criticised aspects of the judgment timeline and says it will pursue lawful remedies.
leaders.implications: The INEC statement is not a final judicial determination of Atiku's eligibility. The outcome depends on the courts and the applicable electoral law.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Coverage must distinguish party allegations, legal arguments and final court decisions; no outcome should be assumed before it is delivered.
leaders.source: The Guardian Nigeria; Channels Television; INEC

leaders.name: Mark Carney
leaders.headline: Canada joins European partners in discussions on Ukraine and security
leaders.report: Canada's prime minister is among leaders attending the Dublin European Political Community summit, with Canada also expected at next week's APEC leaders' meeting in China.
leaders.background: Canada's diplomacy spans transatlantic security, trade, climate and Indo-Pacific partnerships.
leaders.implications: Ottawa's choices will influence cooperation between North America, Europe and Asia-Pacific economies.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Watch for concrete Canadian commitments on Ukraine, trade resilience and regional security rather than summit statements alone.

leaders.name: Vladimir Putin
leaders.headline: Putin meets US envoys but core Ukraine demands remain unresolved
leaders.report: Putin met US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow. Discussions followed Abu Dhabi talks that produced agreement in principle on a prisoner exchange but no peace breakthrough.
leaders.background: Russia continues to oppose European troops in Ukraine and maintains territorial claims rejected by Kyiv and its partners.
leaders.implications: Moscow's position will shape whether negotiations move beyond limited humanitarian arrangements.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Any settlement should be judged by its terms, implementation and respect for Ukraine's sovereignty and international law.

leaders.name: Xi Jinping
leaders.headline: China prepares to host APEC leaders in Shenzhen next week
leaders.report: Xi Jinping is expected to chair the APEC leaders' meeting on 18–19 November, with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin among the leaders expected to attend.
leaders.background: The summit will take place amid technology competition, trade tensions, supply-chain concerns and regional security issues.
leaders.implications: The meeting could influence trade expectations and the tone of US-China engagement, although APEC commitments are voluntary and consensus-based.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Watch for confirmed bilateral meetings and specific commitments; attendance alone does not establish a diplomatic breakthrough.

leaders.name: Volodymyr Zelenskyy
leaders.headline: Zelenskyy seeks meaningful European participation in the next Ukraine talks
leaders.report: Zelenskyy met US envoys in Dublin after their meeting with Putin. He said Europe should have a seat within the next negotiating team, not merely participate separately.
leaders.background: Ukraine continues to reject Russian demands over occupied territory and seeks credible long-term security guarantees.
leaders.implications: The negotiating format will affect the legitimacy and durability of any future settlement.
leaders.radiantWavesView: A durable peace requires Ukraine's meaningful participation, verifiable commitments and protection of civilian security.

leaders.name: Ursula von der Leyen
leaders.headline: EU leaders press for a stronger European role in Ukraine diplomacy
leaders.report: The European Commission president met UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in Dublin ahead of next week's UK-EU summit, while European leaders discussed Ukraine and continental security.
leaders.background: The EU is balancing support for Ukraine with defence coordination, trade relations and resilience against hybrid threats.
leaders.implications: The next summit will show whether European governments can turn broad commitments into practical policy.
leaders.radiantWavesView: Proposals should be assessed by their funding, implementation timetable and measurable effect on security and trade.

leaders.name: Andy Burnham
leaders.position: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom
leaders.headline: UK seeks a practical reset in relations with the European Union
leaders.report: Burnham met Ursula von der Leyen in Dublin and said the UK-EU summit planned for next week could help reduce red tape and costs for businesses and consumers.
leaders.background: The proposed cooperation remains under negotiation and must still be translated into an agreed package.
leaders.implications: A workable UK-EU deal could affect trade, investment, regulatory cooperation and opportunities for young people.
leaders.radiantWavesView: The public should judge the talks by the final text and the practical effects on businesses, prices and mobility.

leaders.name: Cyril Ramaphosa
leaders.headline: African public-health coordination remains vital as insecurity disrupts Ebola response
leaders.report: Africa CDC says attacks on health workers and facilities are undermining containment efforts in eastern DR Congo.
leaders.background: The response requires safe access, contact tracing, community trust and sustained regional coordination.
leaders.implications: The outbreak demonstrates how conflict can undermine health security across borders.
leaders.radiantWavesView: African governments and regional institutions should prioritise safe access for health teams, transparent data and sustained support for affected communities.

leaders.name: Marine Le Pen
leaders.headline: French opposition parties position themselves as social tensions shape the 2027 debate
leaders.report: The cost-of-living debate and continuing talks between the government, unions and employers are likely to shape the political environment ahead of the next presidential election.
leaders.background: Economic policy, public services, immigration and national identity remain central themes in French political competition.
leaders.implications: The evolving debate may influence the direction of French domestic and European policy.
leaders.radiantWavesView: RadiantWaves will distinguish confirmed candidacies and legal developments from campaign speculation and political claims.

opportunities.description: Scholarships for outstanding international students applying for master's and doctoral programmes at French higher-education institutions. Candidates must be nominated by a French institution; applicants do not submit directly to Campus France.
opportunities.eligibility: Master's applicants must be under 29; doctoral applicants under 35 under the 2027 programme rules. French institutions set earlier internal deadlines, so contact the intended institution promptly.

opportunities.title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships 2027/2028
opportunities.organisation: Swiss Confederation / Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students
opportunities.description: Scholarships primarily for early-career researchers from abroad who have already completed a master's degree. The programme is open to applicants from 183 countries, but country-specific procedures and deadlines apply.
opportunities.eligibility: Mainly early-career researchers with a completed master's degree. Applicants must confirm that their nationality and research proposal are eligible and check the deadline with the Swiss representation responsible for their country.
opportunities.deadline: Country-specific — verify with the Swiss representation

opportunities.title: USPF Changemaker Challenge 2026
opportunities.description: Digital-inclusion challenge for innovation teams and early-stage startups developing ICT solutions in agriculture, education, healthcare, financial inclusion or clean energy. National prizes: ₦5 million for first place, ₦3 million for second and ₦2 million for third; finalists also receive incubation support.
opportunities.eligibility: Teams and early-stage startups with practical ICT solutions for underserved communities. Review the challenge rules and submit through the official application platform.

opportunities.title: Young Africa Innovates — Cohort 2
opportunities.location: Abia, Akwa Ibom, Cross River, Katsina, Niger, Plateau and Taraba, Nigeria
opportunities.description: Youth-led innovation programme offering capacity support, bootcamp, incubation, mentorship and potential grant support for ventures addressing real problems in participating states.
opportunities.eligibility: Applicants must be aged 18–35 and resident in one of the seven listed states. Any sector is welcome; reviewers assess problem relevance, proof of concept, scalability and community impact.

opportunities.title: Global EbA Fund — Medium-Size Grants
opportunities.location: Global — ODA-eligible countries, including eligible African contexts
opportunities.description: Grants of up to US$500,000 for innovative, collaborative ecosystem-based adaptation projects. Projects may run for up to 24 months and must address climate resilience, scaling, policy, evidence or investment barriers. The official closing time is 16 November 2026 at 23:59 Pacific Standard Time (17 November at 08:59 Central European Time).
opportunities.eligibility: Legally recognised NGOs, INGOs, community organisations, universities, research institutes, private-sector organisations and consortia. Projects must meet the Fund's EbA criteria, work with local partners and build on existing work. Not an individual scholarship or general business grant.

opportunities.title: 3MTT Delivery Network — Cohort 5 Partner and Funding Applications
opportunities.organisation: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Nigeria
opportunities.description: Registered training organisations can apply for results-based funding to train digital and technical talent. Organisations that do not train can register interest as Opportunity, Funding, Capability, Research and Data, State and Agency, or Amplification Partners.
opportunities.eligibility: For funded delivery-partner applications, the lead must be registered and operating in Nigeria, have recent training delivery evidence and capacity to train at least 100 fellows within six months. RadiantWaves as a media organisation would be more appropriately considered for the Amplification Partner pathway unless it works with an eligible training-provider consortium.

todaysBigQuestion: Should governments require essential public services and critical businesses to maintain tested alternatives when major cloud and communications platforms fail?
thoughtForToday: Digital progress is not measured only by what technology makes possible, but also by how well society can withstand its failure.

radiantWavesPerspective.title: RadiantWaves Perspective: Digital Dependence Must Be Matched by Digital Resilience
radiantWavesPerspective.content: The Microsoft disruption is a reminder that digital convenience can become systemic vulnerability when essential services rely on a narrow group of providers. Governments, hospitals, schools and businesses should test offline procedures, maintain alternative communication channels and demand transparent incident reporting. The same principle applies to energy and public institutions: resilience is measured not only by efficiency, but by the ability to keep essential services running when systems fail.
